title: Adic polynomial approximation for relative derivations of formal power series
statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $m,r\ge0$, $S=F[[t_1,\ldots,t_m]]$ and $T=F[[z_1,\ldots,z_r]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], with variable ideals $\mathfrak a=(t_1,\ldots,t_m)$ and $\mathfrak b=(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$. Let $\psi:S\to T$ be an $F$-algebra homomorphism with $\psi(\mathfrak a)\subseteq\mathfrak b$. Let $E:S\to T$ be an $F$-linear map satisfying $E(uv)=\psi(u)E(v)+\psi(v)E(u)$ for all $u,v\in S$. Write $\partial_j$ for the termwise formal partial derivative [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. Then $E(\mathfrak a^N)\subseteq\mathfrak b^{N-1}$ for every $N\ge1$. For $h\in S$, let $H_N=\sum_{|\alpha|<N}h_\alpha t^\alpha$ be its finite polynomial truncation, regarded in $S$. For every $N\ge1$ and every $j$ one has
$$h-H_N\in\mathfrak a^N,\qquad \partial_j(h-H_N)\in\mathfrak a^{N-1},\qquad E(h-H_N)\in\mathfrak b^{N-1},\qquad\psi(\partial_j(h-H_N))\in\mathfrak b^{N-1}.$$
Moreover
$$E(H_N)=\sum_{j=1}^m\psi(\partial_jH_N)E(t_j),\qquad E(h)-\sum_{j=1}^m\psi(\partial_jh)E(t_j)\in\mathfrak b^{N-1}.$$
The target filtration is separated, $\bigcap_{N\ge0}\mathfrak b^N=0$, and the exact identity is
$$E(h)=\sum_{j=1}^m\psi(\partial_jh)E(t_j).$$
All assertions include $m=0$ or $r=0$; an empty sum is zero.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] with coefficient ring $F$, base ideal $J=0$, and respectively $d=m$ and $d=r$. For $k\ge1$, membership in the variable ideal's $k$th power is equivalent to vanishing of the coefficients of total degree $<k$: the exponents $k-|\alpha|$ are positive, so the required coefficient ideal is $0$. There are finitely many multi-indices of degree $<N$ (each coordinate is $<N$), and $h-H_N$ has all these coefficients zero. Hence $h-H_N\in\mathfrak a^N$. If $v\in\bigcap_{k\ge0}\mathfrak b^k$, its coefficient at any $\beta$ vanishes by taking $k=|\beta|+1$. A power series is its coefficient family [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], so $v=0$. This proves the asserted separatedness, without any completeness theorem.

proof.text:
First $E(1)=E(1\cdot1)=2E(1)$, hence $E(1)=0$ and $F$-linearity gives $E(c)=0$ for $c\in F$. For each $k\ge1$, an element of $\mathfrak a^k$ is a finite sum of products of $k$ elements of $\mathfrak a$; scalar coefficients can be absorbed into the first factor. Thus $\psi(\mathfrak a^k)\subseteq\mathfrak b^k$, and the same inclusion for $k=0$ is automatic. Iterating the given Leibniz rule gives
$$E(u_1\cdots u_N)=\sum_{i=1}^N\left(\prod_{\ell\ne i}\psi(u_\ell)\right)E(u_i).$$
For $u_i\in\mathfrak a$, each summand belongs to $\mathfrak b^{N-1}$; additivity proves $E(\mathfrak a^N)\subseteq\mathfrak b^{N-1}$. In particular this applies to the tail from Step 1. Only finite sums have been differentiated, so no continuity hypothesis has been used.

proof.text:
Put $w=h-H_N$. For $N\ge2$ and $|\alpha|<N-1$, the coefficient formula [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative] gives
$$[t^\alpha]\partial_jw=(\alpha_j+1)[t^{\alpha+e_j}]w=0,$$
since $|\alpha+e_j|<N$. The coefficient criterion of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] with $J=0$ therefore gives $\partial_jw\in\mathfrak a^{N-1}$. For $N=1$ this is membership in $S=\mathfrak a^0$. Step 2 then gives $\psi(\partial_jw)\in\mathfrak b^{N-1}$. Along with Steps 1 and 2 these are all four required tail estimates.

proof.text:
For a monomial $t^\alpha$, induct on $|\alpha|$. The degree-zero case is $E(1)=0$. If $\alpha=\gamma+e_i$, expand $E(t^\gamma t_i)=\psi(t^\gamma)E(t_i)+\psi(t_i)E(t^\gamma)$ and insert the induction formula. The $j=i$ term gains one copy of $\psi(t^\gamma)E(t_i)$; all other exponents are unchanged. Thus
$$E(t^\alpha)=\sum_{j:\alpha_j>0}\alpha_j\psi(t^{\alpha-e_j})E(t_j).$$
The coefficient formula of [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative] identifies $\partial_j(t^\alpha)$ with $\alpha_jt^{\alpha-e_j}$ if $\alpha_j>0$ and with zero otherwise. Multiply by $h_\alpha\in F$ and sum over the finite set $|\alpha|<N$. Linearity and the fact that $\psi$ fixes $F$ give exactly $E(H_N)=\sum_j\psi(\partial_jH_N)E(t_j)$. Integer coefficients mean repeated addition in $F$.

source.place: Tag 0C4B (lemma-fitting-ideal-well-defined), final coordinate-change paragraph, chain rule with details omitted; explicit agent-written adic argument.

proof.text:
Additivity of $E$, $\psi$ and the formal partial derivatives [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative], followed by Step 4, gives
$$E(h)-\sum_j\psi(\partial_jh)E(t_j)=E(w)-\sum_j\psi(\partial_jw)E(t_j).$$
Each term on the right belongs to $\mathfrak b^{N-1}$ by Steps 2 and 3 and closure of an ideal under multiplication and finite sums. The left side is independent of $N$. Taking $N=k+1$ for every $k\ge0$ and applying Step 1 proves it is zero. This gives the exact identity. If $m=0$, $S=F$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $E=0$ by Step 2 and $H_N=h$; there are no partial-derivative clauses. If $r=0$, $T=F$ and $\mathfrak b=0$, and the coefficient/separatedness argument still holds (already $N=2$ gives zero error). The proof also includes $N=1$, where every error bound is in $\mathfrak b^0=T$. No integer was inverted, so positive characteristic is included.

lean.statement: theorem formal_relative_derivation_expansion (F : Type u) [Field F] (m r : ℕ) (ψ : MvPowerSeries (Fin m) F →ₐ[F] MvPowerSeries (Fin r) F) (E : MvPowerSeries (Fin m) F →ₗ[F] MvPowerSeries (Fin r) F) (hψ : ∀ f : MvPowerSeries (Fin m) F, f ∈ Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin m → MvPowerSeries (Fin m) F)) → ψ f ∈ Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin r → MvPowerSeries (Fin r) F))) (hE : ∀ f g : MvPowerSeries (Fin m) F, E (f * g) = ψ f * E g + ψ g * E f) : (∀ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N → ∀ f : MvPowerSeries (Fin m) F, f ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin m → MvPowerSeries (Fin m) F))) ^ N → E f ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin r → MvPowerSeries (Fin r) F))) ^ (N - 1)) ∧ (∀ (h : MvPowerSeries (Fin m) F) (N : ℕ), 1 ≤ N → (h - (truncTotal N h : MvPowerSeries (Fin m) F) ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin m → MvPowerSeries (Fin m) F))) ^ N) ∧ (∀ j : Fin m, pderiv F j (h - (truncTotal N h : MvPowerSeries (Fin m) F)) ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin m → MvPowerSeries (Fin m) F))) ^ (N - 1)) ∧ (E (h - (truncTotal N h : MvPowerSeries (Fin m) F)) ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin r → MvPowerSeries (Fin r) F))) ^ (N - 1)) ∧ (∀ j : Fin m, ψ (pderiv F j (h - (truncTotal N h : MvPowerSeries (Fin m) F))) ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin r → MvPowerSeries (Fin r) F))) ^ (N - 1)) ∧ (E (truncTotal N h : MvPowerSeries (Fin m) F) = ∑ j : Fin m, ψ (pderiv F j (truncTotal N h : MvPowerSeries (Fin m) F)) * E (X j)) ∧ (E h - ∑ j : Fin m, ψ (pderiv F j h) * E (X j) ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin r → MvPowerSeries (Fin r) F))) ^ (N - 1))) ∧ (⨅ N : ℕ, (Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin r → MvPowerSeries (Fin r) F))) ^ N) = ⊥ ∧ (∀ h : MvPowerSeries (Fin m) F, E h = ∑ j : Fin m, ψ (pderiv F j h) * E (X j))
